FORMAT: no translucent/fading element detected, so GIF can represent this asset faithfully and is a legitimate choice on compatibility grounds. WebP/AVIF still keep real antialiasing on the silhouette instead of dithering it, and need far less per-asset flag tuning. Ranking:
  full resolution -> WebP lossless (bit-exact, widest support), then AVIF q85 (smaller, still excellent), then GIF.
  under a byte cap (e.g. 256 KB emoji) -> AVIF first: measured, it keeps EVERY frame where WebP and GIF each drop a third to two-thirds. Then WebP, then GIF.
  maximum compatibility -> WebP, then GIF, then AVIF.
  Prefer GIF only when the destination requires it, or when it is a genuine win on size or render time at near-equal visual quality. Always report frame counts alongside file sizes -- under a cap, frames are what actually gets spent.

A SOLID art colour sits 57 from the background, inside the default feather band (15..60) -- it would be given partial alpha and dithered away in a GIF even though it is not the background. Recommending --feather-band-multiplier 3.3 so the band stops short of it while still reaching 50, far enough to keep removing the antialiasing ramp. (For a WebP/AVIF output this cannot happen: --recover-fade-alpha identifies it as a solid palette colour and keeps it opaque. See references/lessons.md SS16.)

250 TRANSIENT small removed region(s) observed (largest 200px) -- recommending --erosion-exempt-max-size 221 to protect them from erosion inflation. 0 further small region(s) were seen in ~every frame at a stable size and are treated as DESIGN, not incidental noise, so they are excluded from this suggestion.

Region 1: enclosure_ratio 0.8 over 383px (0.6% of the canvas) -- left as background. It clears neither bar: 0.9 enclosure at any size, or 0.5 enclosure at 2.5%+ of the canvas. ⚠️ If this region is visibly part of the ARTWORK, protect it by hand (--protect-outline-color / --protect-region) -- this verdict has been wrong on a large pale region before.

Region 2: if this enclosed interior is BACKGROUND rather than design (a gap showing through a lattice, the white inside a sparkle), protecting it is the wrong answer and no protection flag can express that. Add --unprotect-region rect:94,56,70,89 to re-key it as background while leaving the artwork there untouched. ⚠️ THIS BOX IS A STARTING POINT, not a measured answer: it is this region's extent on the SAMPLED frame, and an interior that grows across the animation will leave residue outside it -- widen it and re-check. Widen deliberately: measured on one asset, a 15% pad cleared the residue but reached the artwork's outer silhouette and trimmed 1,287 px of it. A STATIC BOX IS THE WRONG SHAPE IF THE INTERIOR MOVES: --remove-region-track takes this same spec as a frame-0 SEED and follows the region by continuity instead (--remove-region-track rect:94,56,70,89), which is the answer when the hole drifts, rotates or is periodically occluded -- measured on a real asset, a static box hit the target on 1 of 24 frames and the tracker on 24 of 24 (references/lessons.md SS33). ⚠️ Seed the COMPONENT, not this box, if the box covers more than one same-coloured blob: a candidate region is grouped by canvas proximity, not by per-frame connectivity, so one region id can hold a hole to punch AND decoration to keep. --recover-fade-alpha ignores every PROTECTION flag, but composes with all three region flags here (--unprotect-region, --remove-region, --remove-region-track), so "fade the glow AND remove the white inside" is one command either way (references/lessons.md SS43, SS48). NOT applied automatically: whether an interior is design or background is the user's call, not something the pixels answer -- this region encloses on 71% of 144 frames, which is why it is being asked about at all.
